description: Default capability for the main window. Vault access pattern: the user picks a vault folder at runtime via the dialog plugin; fs calls are then scoped to that folder by the web layer. V1 DEV ONLY: the fs scope below is a blanket $HOME/** grant so any picked vault works. $APPDATA is listed SEPARATELY because Tauri's scope globs never cross dot-directories — $HOME/** does NOT match ~/.local/... — and the durable stores (M1) live under app-data; without these entries every desktop vault boot fails with 'forbidden path' on its store dir. For the same reason <vault>/.ohhi/ (custom themes, app files) and <vault>/.obsidian/ (daily-notes.json) get their own $HOME/**/.ohhi and $HOME/**/.obsidian entries: a literal leading-dot segment in the pattern matches, where ** alone does not (spike-resource-root F0; unverified on a real desktop build, and a vault under another dot-directory is still refused). $CONFIG/ohhi is the user resource root (layouts, later keymaps and templates; quiet-shell F8, spike-resource-root Q4) — ~/.config/ohhi on Linux, read-only from the app; also unverified on a real build. TODO(tighten before real dogfooding): replace the $HOME grant with tauri-plugin-persisted-scope or runtime-scoped grants keyed to the picked folder — see plans/shaping.md D6. Updater: check, download and install (not the download-and-install shortcut), plus process:allow-restart to relaunch into an installed update. The feed URL and signing key live in tauri.conf.json, so the webview can neither repoint the updater nor make it accept an unsigned build.
